info.description:
For questions, contact us at MS Teams or Discord: herecity

### Authentication

All API requests must be authenticated. Include your `apiUser` and an MD5 hash of your `apiKey` in the JSON body of every request. You can set these values once in this collection's 'Variables' tab for ease of use.

**Example Authentication Fields:**

``` json
{
  "apiUser": "{{apiUser}}",
  "apiKey": "{{apiKey}}"
}

 ```

item.name: Private Manual Orders

request.description:
Creates a private Manual order on the receiving EA account. amount is in thousands of coins: 500 means 500,000 coins. user is the receiving account email; pass requires at least 8 characters; ba is the required backup code (at least 6 characters, not 0). Optional ba2-ba5 supply additional backup codes. platform is PS, XB or PC. customerName and externalOrderID are optional labels.

Save the returned orderID in manualOrderId. The saved settings are ready before onboarding begins; the order proceeds automatically after onboarding. This request creates a real order when sent to a deployed endpoint.

### Manual settings

| Field | Values / default |
| --- | --- |
| manualBuyVisibility | private only (default); public and portal publication are rejected |
| manualBuySubMode | fresh (default), rotate, lockFirst, manual |
| manualBuyPlayerResourceID | Required positive resource ID for manual |
| manualBuyMinRating / manualBuyMaxRating | 79-84; defaults 82/84; minimum must not exceed maximum |
| manualBuyMaxBuyPrice | 100-15000000 coins; default 1000 |
| manualBuyListPrice | 200-15000000 coins; default 3800 |
| manualBuyStartPriceMode | dynamic (default) or fixed |
| manualBuyStartPriceFixed | Required for fixed; 150-15000000 and below list price |
| manualBuyCyclesPerPlayer | For rotate: 1-1000; default 20 |
| manualBuyListingDurationSeconds | 3600, 10800 (default), 21600, 43200 |
| manualBuyParallelListings | 1-90; default 1. Legacy Normal-mode concurrency limit; an active/paused steady pool ignores it |
| manualBuyPoolMode | disabled (default), active or paused; the optional steady pool |
| manualBuyAvailableTarget | 1-90; default 1. Independent of manualBuyParallelListings - a target above the parallel cap is a valid pair, and the receiver's fresh transfer-list capacity gate enforces the physical ceiling |

Manual selection mode chooses the card; private visibility keeps it out of the public marketplace. Configuration is a complete settings submission: omitted settings use defaults, rather than preserving their old values.

Send a JSON object with Content-Type: application/json. Use the existing apiUser and apiKey variables; apiKey is the MD5 hash used by this collection. Access is limited to orders created by that API account. Unknown and foreign orders return the same 404. Public marketplace and portal-published orders are not supported here. Responses use an HTTP status and matching JSON code. No receiver credentials are returned.

request.description:
Turns the target-only steady pool back on and keeps up to availableTarget UNCLAIMED cards AVAILABLE for buyers. Cards a buyer already holds (locked/pendingVerification) and cards parked for review (buyerReview) are reserved for the order and still occupy the receiving account, but they do not count against availableTarget, so four claimed cards of a target of 20 still refill four. maxConcurrent is the legacy Normal-mode concurrency limit: it is stored and returned, and an active/paused pool ignores it entirely.

availableTarget and maxConcurrent are optional: omit them to keep the saved values, or send either one to change it. availableTarget is validated 1..90 and is INDEPENDENT of maxConcurrent - a target above the parallel cap (for example 90 with a cap of 1) is a valid pair, and activating a saved pair such as target 20 / cap 4 is accepted without asking for a new target. request.description:
Report a purchase of a card you claimed on this order. emailHash is the 32-character MD5 hex digest of the buying EA account email. A success means pendingVerification, not a settled delivery; the receiver verifies the sale. The pending marker, the wake-up signal and the queue TTL are published as one atomic Redis transaction, so a receiver that consumes the signal immediately does not make a delivered report look failed. A success publishes the signal; it does not hold the card until the next poll, because the receiver may verify and advance or release the auction first.

On 503 the publication could not be confirmed, which does not prove the notification was lost: re-read the listing status, repeat the identical request with the same orderID, transactionID and emailHash only while the card is still held or pending, and never claim or buy the card again. A different emailHash or an already settled claim returns 409. Read listing states to follow verification.

item.description:
Use your own suppliers to buy cards listed on the receiving EA account of your own order. All four endpoints use apiUser/apiKey authentication and enforce order ownership. No public marketplace stock or other owners' orders are returned.

### Setup and flow
1. Set base_url to the main API site, apiUser to your owner account, and apiKey to the existing MD5 API credential. These are not cocoin portal endpoints.
2. Set manualReceiverEmail, manualReceiverPassword and manualReceiverBackupCode locally. Create an order, then copy its orderID to manualOrderId.
3. Poll Get Order Player Listings, or Get Order Player Listings - Multiple Orders to search up to 25 of your own orders in one request (poll with one request in flight, back off when a page is empty, and start each refresh from cursor 0). Copy a transactionID to manualTransactionId, and when the result came from a batch also use the card orderID, then claim that card.
4. Have your supplier buy that exact EA auction. Set manualBuyerEmailHash and report bought, or cancel an unpurchased claim.
5. Re-read listing states to observe verification. Never share your owner API key with suppliers; an existing order-specific supplier link is the direct-access alternative.

Examples are templates, not proof of a live deployment. This additive API must be deployed and staging-verified before use. It requires JSON POST bodies and returns JSON with matching HTTP/code statuses. Generic errors: 400 invalid input, 403 invalid credentials, 404 unknown/foreign order or card, 405 wrong method, 409 ineligible state, 415 non-JSON content, 429 receiver throttle, 500 server failure, 503 retryable service failure. Initial start/conversion is intentionally restricted; executed orders use the existing recovery process.

request.description:
Creates an order to buy coins from a specific supplier or the public pool.

### Request Body

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `supplierID` | String | Conditional | The ID of the supplier. **Required for `snipe` method.** Optional for `snipeLimited` (omit to use pool mode). |
| `privateSupplier` | String | No | `1` for a private supplier, `0` for public. Default `0`. |
| `externalOrderID` | String | No | Your custom internal ID for this order. |
| `playerToBuy` | Integer | No | Resource ID of a specific player to buy (auto-calculates amount based on player price). |
| `maxPrice` | Float | No | Maximum price per 100K you're willing to pay. Rejects supplier if price exceeds this. |
| `transferMethod` | String | No | Transfer method to use. Values: `snipe` (default), `cycle`, `targetedSnipe`, `snipeLimited`. |
| `buyNowThreshold` | Float | Conditional | Price threshold per 100K. **Required for `cycle` and `targetedSnipe` methods.** For `snipeLimited` pool mode, this sets the max price per 100K (only accounts priced at or below this value will be used). |
| `topUpEnabled` | Integer | No | Only for `targetedSnipe` method. Top-up threshold in K (e.g., `150` = 150K minimum coins before top-up triggers). `0`: Disabled. Defaults to `150` for targetedSnipe. Valid range: 0-9999. Automatically disabled for cycle methods. |
| `autoFinishCycle` | Integer | No | Only for `targetedSnipe` method. `1`: When order amount reaches limit, finish remaining via cycle method. `0`: Disabled (default). |
| `minTransferAmount` | Integer | No | Minimum coins per transfer in K (e.g., 50 = 50K). Only for `targetedSnipe` method. When a transfer would be below this amount, behavior depends on `pauseIfBelowMinTransfer`. |
| `pauseIfBelowMinTransfer` | Integer | No | Behavior when transfer is below `minTransferAmount`. `0` (default): Switch to cycle mode. `1`: Pause the order with `economyState = 'belowMinTransfer'`. |
| `riskLevel` | Integer | No | Safety/risk level for `targetedSnipe` method. `1`: Maximum (lowest capacity), `2`: Safe (higher capacity, **default**), `3`: Low Ban Risk - no refunds (increased capacity), `4`: Medium Ban Risk - no refunds (even higher capacity), `5`: Increased Ban Risk - no refunds (highest capacity), `6`: Ban Mode - no refunds (unlimited capacity). |
| *...other fields* |  |  | All parameters from the **Submit Order** endpoint are also applicable (customerName, user, pass, ba, ba2-ba5, platform, amount, persona, updateCustomer, etc.). |

### Transfer Methods

| Method | Description | Amount Limits | Requires supplierID |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `snipe` | Standard snipe transfer (default) | No specific limits | Yes |
| `cycle` | cycle method | Min: 1K, Max: 1.5M | No (optional for private supplier) |
| `targetedSnipe` | Surgical snipe with specific player targeting (2.0x multiplier) | Min: 6K | No |
| `snipeLimited` | Limited snipe method. Without `supplierID`/`privateSupplier`: uses **pool mode** (public seller pool, `buyNowThreshold` = max price). With `privateSupplier=1` + `supplierID`: uses a specific private supplier. | No specific limits | No (pool mode) / Optional (private supplier) |

### Rate Limiting

Customer accounts are rate-limited to prevent spam:
- Max 3 orders per minute (burst protection)
- Max 10 orders per 5 minutes
- Max 30 orders per 30 minutes

### Responses

- **200 OK:** Order created successfully. Returns `{"orderID": "uuid"}`
- **400 Bad Request:** Missing or invalid parameters (supplierNotFound, supplierOverpriced, Invalid JSON, etc.)
- **402 Insufficient Funds:** You do not have enough balance to purchase.
- **403 Forbidden:** API authentication failed or order creation blocked.
- **406 Not Acceptable:** The selected supplier has insufficient stock.
- **429 Too Many Requests:** Rate limit exceeded or account submitted too recently.

request.description:
Retrieves the detailed status of a single order. Can query by `orderID`, `externalID`, or `motherOrderID`.

### Request Body

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orderID` | String | Yes | The ID of the order to query. |
| `apiUser` | String | Yes | Your API user email. |
| `apiKey` | String | Yes | MD5 hash of your API key. |
| `externalID` | Integer | No | Set to `1` if `orderID` is your custom `externalOrderID`. |
| `isMotherID` | Integer | No | Set to `1` if `orderID` is a `motherOrderID` from an auto-buy order. Returns aggregated results for all child orders. |

### Response Body

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | String | Overall order status (e.g., `partlyDelivered`, `finished`). |
| `accountCheck` | String | Detailed onboarding status code. |
| `economyState` | String | Detailed transfer process status code. |
| `amountOrdered` | Integer | The total amount of coins ordered (in K). |
| `amount` | Integer | The amount of coins delivered so far (in K). |
| `coinsUsed` | Integer | Total coins taken from sender accounts. |
| `coinsCustomerAccount` | Integer | Last known coin balance of the customer's account. |
| `toPay` | Float | The cost of the order (for buy orders). |
| `sellerReceives` | Float | Amount the seller receives (for buy orders). |
| `externalOrderID` | String | Your custom ID for the order, if provided. |
| `wasAborted` | Integer | `1` if the order was aborted, `0` otherwise. |
| `knownClub` | String | The customer's club name, if known. |
| `ba1`\-`ba5` | String | _(Returned only to authorized users)_ The customer's backup codes. |
| `cached` | Integer | `1` if the response is from cache, `0` otherwise. |

| **Output** | **Description** | **Possible Values** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Status | Overall status of the order | ready, entered, partlyDelivered,finished, waitingForAssignment, interrupted |
| AccountCheck | Status of the onboarding of the account, only on finished accountCheck the order can start | wrongBA, noClub, wrongConsole, tlFull, notEnoughCoins, finished, entered, started, noUnassignedItemsPresent, userPassVerified, correctBA, noTM, console, FailedProxyConnectionError, wrongUserPass, loginFailed, FailedProxyPoolExhausted, unassignedItemsPresent, noUnassignedItemsPresent, captcha, wrongPersona,LoginFailedDeviceBan |
| EconomyState | Detailed transactions status | FailNoClubToCanBeEAErrorTryAgain, FailedWrongCredentialsTo, FailedWrongBACodeTo, FailWebAppCustomerLocked, FailLoggedInConsoleTo, insufficientFunds, calcErrorMaintenance, noPlayer, noSuitableSender, entered, started, transfersInProgress, transferCycleComplete, customerHasPlayer, customerListedPlayer, finished, FailedReceiverDeviceBan, FailedSessionExpiredCustomerLoggedIn?, FailedTLfullReceiver, FailWebAppNotYetUnlocked, belowMinTransfer |

Handling of return codes during onboarding:

- **`wrongPersona`****:** The user needs to switch their persona or provide the correct persona information, and then they can attempt the process again.
    
- **`captcha`****:** The user is required to solve the captcha, after which they can retry the process.
    
- **`unassignedItemsPresent`****:** The user must remove unassigned items from their account so that the count is below 50, and then they can retry the process.
    
- **`FailedProxyPoolExhausted`****:** This is a legacy issue and is no longer used. The user can proceed with retrying the process.
    
- **`notEnoughCoins`****:** The user needs to have more than 1500 coins in their account balance. After meeting this requirement, they can retry the process.
    
- **`tlFull`****:** The user should ensure that there are at least 3 available slots in both their transfer list and transfer targets. After making these adjustments, they can retry the process.
    
- **`FailedProxyConnectionError`****:** This is a technical error related to proxy connections. The user is allowed to retry the process.
    
- **`noClub`****:** This indicates that the account is not usable due to the absence of a club. The user can retry the process.
    
- **`console`****:** This means the user needs to log out from the console. After doing so, they can retry the process.
    
- **`wrongConsole`****:** This suggests that there is an issue with the order type. It needs to be corrected either by the user or by submitting a different account.
    
- **`loginFailed`****:** This could be a temporary login issue. The user can retry the process.
    
- **`wrongUserPass`****:** The user needs to use a new combination of username and password, and then they can retry the process.
    
- **`wrongBA`****:** The user needs to obtain a new backup code and use it. After doing so, they can retry the process.
    
- **`noTM`****:** This indicates that the account does not have access to the transfer market. The user needs to submit a different account for the process.
    
- **`belowMinTransfer`****:** The calculated transfer amount is below the configured `minTransferAmount`. This occurs when `pauseIfBelowMinTransfer=1` was set on the order. The user can either: (1) resume the order to continue with a smaller transfer, (2) wait for more coins to accumulate, or (3) convert to cycle method.

request.description:
Converts a `targetedSnipe` order to `cycle` method and resumes it. This is useful when a targeted snipe order is interrupted and you want to complete the remaining amount using the faster cycle method.

### Request Body

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orderID` | String | Yes | The UUID of the order to convert. Must be a valid UUID v4 format. |
| `apiUser` | String | Yes | Your API user email. |
| `apiKey` | String | Yes | MD5 hash of your API key. |

### Validation Rules

- Only `targetedSnipe` orders can be converted to cycle
    
- Order must be in an interrupted/error state (e.g., `interrupted`, `noPlayer`, `insufficientFunds`, etc.)
    
- Cannot convert orders with temp bans (`FailPlayerLostToTempban`, `FailListTempBanCustomer`)
    
- Pending amount must be at least 1K and maximum 2,500K (2.5M coins)
    

### Response Body

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `orderID` | String | The order ID that was converted. |
| `newSellMode` | String | The new sell mode (`cycle`). |
| `pendingAmount` | Integer | Remaining amount to transfer (in K). |

### Responses

- **200 OK:** Order successfully converted to cycle method.
    
- **400 Bad Request:** Invalid order ID format, order not in valid state, or order type cannot be converted.
    
- **403 Forbidden:** Invalid API credentials.
    
- **404 Not Found:** Order not found or access denied.

request.description:
Updates order parameters such as amount, price limit, sort mode, cycle price, and transfer settings. Supports partial updates — only provided fields are changed.

### Request Body

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `orderID` | String | Yes | The UUID of the order to edit. |
| `apiUser` | String | Yes | Your API user email. |
| `apiKey` | String | Yes | MD5 hash of your API key. |
| `amount` | Integer | No | New amount in K (e.g., `500` for 500K). Cannot be less than already transferred amount. |
| `limit` | Integer | No | New player price limit. |
| `sortMode` | Integer | No | New sort mode value. |
| `cyclePrice` | Float | No | New price per 100K for cycle/targetedSnipe orders. Must be > 0. Only applicable to `cycle` and `targetedSnipe` sell modes. |
| `minTransferAmount` | Integer | No | Minimum coins per transfer in K (0-9999). Only applied to cycle orders (`cycle`, `targetedSnipe`). |
| `pauseIfBelowMinTransfer` | Integer | No | `0`: Switch to cycle mode when below min. `1`: Pause the order. Only applied to cycle orders. |
| `topUpEnabled` | Integer | No | Top-up threshold in K (0-9999). Only applied to `targetedSnipe` orders. |
| `riskLevel` | Integer | No | Safety/risk level for `targetedSnipe` orders. `1`-`10` set the card limit per recipient within the 36h tracking window (default `4` on submit). `11`: Ban Mode (unlimited capacity, no refunds). Higher values increase capacity but raise ban risk. Only applied to `targetedSnipe` orders. |

**Note:** At least one optional field must be provided in addition to the required fields. Fields that don't apply to the order's sell mode are silently ignored (e.g., `topUpEnabled` on a `cycle` order, `minTransferAmount` on a `snipe` order).

### Validation Rules

- `amount` cannot be set below the already-transferred amount (`lowAmount` error)
- `amount` cannot be reduced while a transfer is actively in progress (`transferRunning` error)
- If `amount` is increased on orders with `viewRights`, stock availability and balance are verified
- `cyclePrice` returns `cyclePriceNotAllowed` if the order is not a cycle/targetedSnipe type
- `cyclePrice` returns `orderFinished` if the order status is `finished`

### Response Body

| Field | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `outcome` | String | `success` if the update was applied. |
| `updatedFields` | Array | List of field names that were actually updated (e.g., `["amount", "limit", "cyclePrice"]`). |

### Responses

- **200 OK:** `{"outcome": "success", "updatedFields": ["amount", "limit"]}`
- **400 Bad Request:** Invalid input, missing fields, `lowAmount`, `transferRunning`, `cyclePriceNotAllowed`, or `orderFinished`.
- **402 Payment Required:** `insufficientBalance` — not enough balance to cover the new amount.
- **403 Forbidden:** Invalid API credentials.
- **404 Not Found:** `orderNotFound` — order does not exist or you don't have access.
- **406 Not Acceptable:** `insufficientStock` — supplier doesn't have enough stock for the increased amount.
- **429 Too Many Requests:** Rate limited for repeated invalid requests.

request.description:
Retrieves before/after balance snapshots for orders or individual transfers. Returns a JPEG image.

### Query Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `orderID` | String | Conditional | The order ID to get screenshots for. Required if `transferID` not provided. |
| `transferID` | String | Conditional | The individual transfer ID. Required if `orderID` not provided. |
| `mode` | Integer | Yes | The type of screenshot to retrieve (see modes below). |

### Screenshot Modes

| Mode | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `1` | **Before Snapshot** - Regular orders use the first finished transfer. Manual `externalSell` orders use the earliest recorded nonempty before image across their real receiver sessions. |
| `2` | **After Snapshot** - Regular orders use the last finished transfer. Manual `externalSell` orders use the latest recorded nonempty after image across their real receiver sessions. |
| `3` | **Squad Before** - Squad screenshot before (for SBC-related orders). |
| `4` | **Squad After** - Squad screenshot after (for SBC-related orders). |
| `5` | **Manual Before** - Existing individual-launcher manual before route. |

### Manual Orders

Manual snapshots are account balance history, not proof that each listed card sold or that the order completed. Failed, expired and in-progress receiver sessions remain eligible because the image belongs to the original launcher session. Superseded, switched-player and stopped-after-onboarding bookkeeping rows are excluded.

### Authentication

Supports both session-based authentication (for GUI) and API authentication:
- **API Authentication**: Include `apiUser` and `apiKey` in the JSON body.
- **Session Authentication**: Must be logged in via the web interface.

### Access Control

- Admins can access all screenshots.
- Regular users can only access screenshots for orders they created (`externalOrderCreator`) or have view rights to (`viewRights`).

### Response

- **Success**: Returns a JPEG image (`Content-Type: image/jpeg`).
- **Missing image**: Returns generic `404 Screenshot not found.` text when no usable stored image exists. It does not call a legacy screenshot host with a missing transfer ID or blank filename.
- **Upstream failure**: Returns generic `504` timeout or `502` provider text without exposing hosts, credentials, cURL errors or provider diagnostics.

Provides stock availability preview for both Buy Coins and New Order modes. Supports two modes: Stock at Price (given maxPrice) and Price for Stock (given requiredStock).

### Mode 1: Stock at Price (maxPrice provided)

Calculates how much stock is available at a given price threshold.

### Mode 2: Price for Stock (requiredStock provided)

Finds the minimum price required to fulfill a specific stock amount (includes 15% buffer).

### Request Body

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `apiUser` | String | Yes | Your API user email. |
| `apiKey` | String | Yes | MD5 hash of your API key. |
| `platform` | String | Yes | Gaming platform: `PS`, `XB`, or `PC`. |
| `transferMethod` | String | No | Transfer method: `targetedSnipe`, `cycle`, `snipeLimited`. Defaults to `cycle`. |
| `ownSenders` | Integer | No | `1` for your own sender accounts (New Order), `0` for external sellers (Buy Coins). Defaults to `0`. |
| `maxPrice` | Float | Conditional | Price threshold per 100K. Required for external sellers in Mode 1. |
| `minAmount` | Integer | No | Minimum coins per account in K. Defaults to `0`. |
| `requiredStock` | Float | Conditional | Required stock amount in coins (e.g., `500000` for 500K). Use for Mode 2. |

### Response (Mode 1 - Stock at Price)

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "totalStock": "850K",
  "totalStockRaw": 850000,
  "accountCount": 15,
  "sellerCount": 3,
  "available": "650K",
  "availableRaw": 650000,
  "top10Count": 10
}
```

### Response (Mode 2 - Price for Stock, can fulfill)

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "canFulfill": true,
  "requiredStock": 500000,
  "suggestedPrice": 8.63,
  "stockAtPrice": 520000
}
```

### Response (Mode 2 - Price for Stock, cannot fulfill)

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "canFulfill": false,
  "requiredStock": 500000,
  "maxAvailableStock": 300000,
  "maxAvailablePrice": 10.35
}
```

### Notes

- For external sellers (`ownSenders: 0`), `maxPrice` is required.
- The `top10Count` and detailed stock info may only be visible to admin users.
- Uses fast aggregation queries for performance.

request.description:
Returns real-time market feedback. Provides different insights depending on the caller's role (buyer or seller) and the selected trading mode.

### Request Body

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `apiUser` | String | Yes | Your API user email. |
| `apiKey` | String | Yes | MD5 hash of your API key. |
| `role` | String | No | `buyer` (default) or `seller`. Determines the response type. |
| `price` | Float | Yes | The price per 100K to evaluate. Use `0` for distribution-only requests in `targeted` mode. |
| `platform` | String | No | `PS` (default), `XB`, or `PC`. `PS` and `XB` share the same console stock pool. |
| `priceCurrency` | String | No | `EUR` (default) or `USD`. Prices are converted internally for comparison. |
| `amount` | Integer | No | Order size in 100K units (e.g. `20` = 2M coins). Defaults to `20`. Only used for buyer coverage calculation. |
| `mode` | String | No | `cycle` (default), `pool`, or `targeted`. Determines which market data is returned. |

### Response — Buyer (cycle / pool)

```json
{
  "hasStock": true,
  "coverage": "enough"
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `hasStock` | Boolean | Whether any sender accounts are available at the given price. |
| `coverage` | String | _(Optional)_ Stock coverage relative to order size: `enough`, `tight`, `limited`, or `none`. Omitted when the sender pool summary is missing from cache — the response will be just `{"hasStock": false}`. |

### Response — Seller (cycle / pool)

```json
{
  "hasRecentData": true,
  "demandLevel": "high",
  "competitiveness": "competitive",
  "avgFillPrice": 5.25
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `hasRecentData` | Boolean | Whether recent market data exists. |
| `demandLevel` | String | Current trading activity level (upstream enum; defaults to `low` when the cache is empty). |
| `competitiveness` | String | _(Only when `hasRecentData: true`)_ How your price compares to recent fills: `too_cheap`, `competitive`, `at_market`, or `above_market`. |
| `avgFillPrice` | Float | _(Only when `hasRecentData: true`)_ Average recent transaction price per 100K (in your requested currency). |

### Additional Seller Fields — `cycle` mode only

When `role=seller` and `mode=cycle`, the response may include a live stock distribution across price brackets. These fields appear in addition to the core seller fields above.

```json
{
  "hasRecentData": true,
  "demandLevel": "high",
  "competitiveness": "at_market",
  "avgFillPrice": 5.25,
  "hasDistribution": true,
  "distribution": [
    { "from": 5.0, "to": 5.05, "level": "very_high", "stock": 2400000 },
    { "from": 5.05, "to": 5.1, "level": "high", "stock": 1600000 }
  ],
  "priceMin": 5.0,
  "priceMax": 5.5,
  "cheaperPercent": 40
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `hasDistribution` | Boolean | Present only when live cycle stock data is available. |
| `distribution` | Array | Price brackets with relative stock levels. `stock` is fillable coin volume at that price tier. |
| `priceMin` / `priceMax` | Float | Bracket range of the returned distribution (in your requested currency). |
| `cheaperPercent` | Integer | _(Optional)_ Percentage of coin volume priced at or below your price. Only returned when `price > 0`. |

### Response — Targeted mode

```json
{
  "hasData": true,
  "distribution": [
    { "from": 4.5, "to": 4.55, "level": "very_high", "stock": 120 },
    { "from": 4.55, "to": 4.6, "level": "high", "stock": 80 }
  ],
  "priceMin": 4.5,
  "priceMax": 6.0,
  "cheaperPercent": 35
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `hasData` | Boolean | Whether distribution data is available. |
| `distribution` | Array | Price brackets with relative stock levels (`very_high`, `high`, `medium`, `low`). |
| `priceMin` | Float | Lowest price in the distribution range. |
| `priceMax` | Float | Highest price in the distribution range. |
| `cheaperPercent` | Integer | _(Optional)_ Percentage of stock priced below your price. Only returned when `price > 0`. |

### Error Responses

All errors still return HTTP `200` with a JSON body containing an `error` key.

| Body | When |
| :--- | :--- |
| `{"hasRecentData": false, "error": "invalid_price"}` | `price` is negative, or `price` is `0` outside `targeted` mode. |
| `{"hasStock": false, "hasRecentData": false, "error": "redis_unavailable"}` | Redis is unreachable. |
| `{"hasData": false}` | `targeted` mode with no cached cumulative stock. |

request.description:
Submits a task to buy specific players from the transfer market onto an account. The system logs in to the account, searches for each player, and purchases them at market price (or your specified max price).

The `baseID` and card version are resolved automatically from the player database — you only need to provide the `resourceID` (the `player_id` field from **Get All Players**). Untradeable SBC-only cards are rejected, as they cannot be bought on the market.

### Request Body

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `account` | String | Yes | The account email to buy the players on. Must belong to the API user. |
| `accountType` | String | Yes | The type of account. Values: `sender`, `customer`. |
| `players` | Array | Yes | An array of player objects (limit 50 per task). Duplicate entries are allowed and buy multiple copies. |
| `players[].resourceID` | Integer | Yes | The resource ID of the exact card to buy (`player_id` from **Get Available Players**). |
| `players[].maxPrice` | Integer | No | Maximum coins to pay for this player (150 - 15,000,000). If omitted, the player is bought at market price. |
| `moveToClub` | Integer | No | `1` to move bought players to the club, `0` to leave them on the transfer list. Defaults to `1`. |
| `consoleLock` | Integer | No | `1` to lock the console during the task. Defaults to `0`. |

### Responses
*   **200 OK:** Returns the created task with its `buyTaskID`. Use this ID with **Query Buy Players Status (Bulk)**.
*   **400 Bad Request:** Invalid input, unknown `resourceID`, untradeable SBC card, or the account does not belong to the API user.
*   **403 Forbidden:** `invalidCredentials`.

Requests an immediate refresh of a sender account's status (e.g., coin balance).

**Note:** Refresh requests are rate-limited. You can only request a refresh if the last one was more than 2 minutes ago and no refresh is currently ongoing.

Manually updates the coin balance and status of a sender account without requiring a full refresh. This is useful if you update the balance externally.

### Request Body

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `user` | String | Yes | The email of the sender account. |
| `coins` | Integer | Yes | The new coin balance. |
| `action` | String | No | Performs a direct DB update. Values: `stop`, `resume`. If omitted, the update is queued unless `clearBan` is `true`. |
| `toUse` | Integer | No | New amount of coins (in K) available for transfer. |
| `resetToUse`| Integer | No | If `1`, resets the `takenSession` counter for the account. Defaults to `0`. |
| `clearBan` | Boolean | No | Defaults to `false`. Set to `true` to clear a local ban marker during a direct coin update. Must be a JSON boolean; strings, numbers and null are rejected. |

With `clearBan: true`, processing happens directly using the existing account permissions. Only `usedByWorker` values containing the case-sensitive substring `ban` are cleared; other worker assignments are preserved. This does not lift an EA restriction. Without `action`, pause flags remain unchanged. With `action: "resume"`, `isUseless` is also set to `0`; `stopped` and reservations remain unchanged.

### Responses

*   **200 OK:** Update successful/queued.
*   **404 Not Found:** Account not found.
*   **400 Bad Request:** Invalid input, including a non-boolean `clearBan`.

| `transactionID` | Integer | Internal listing ID. Use this in the Status endpoint. |
| `tradeID` | String | Trade ID to search for. |
| `resourceID` | Integer | Resource ID of the player. |
| `playerName` | String | Player name. |
| `rating` | Integer | Player overall rating. |
| `startPrice` | Integer | Listing start price. |
| `buyNowPrice` | Integer | Buy-now price for this auction. |
| `platform` | String | `cons` or `pc`. |
| `lockExpires` | Integer | Unix timestamp when your lock expires. |
| `balance` | Float | Your current balance. |

request.description:
Reports the outcome of a locked listing.

### Request Body

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `apiUser`, `apiKey` | String | Yes | Authentication credentials. |
| `transactionID` | Integer | Yes | The `transactionID` from **Get Player Listing**. |
| `status` | String | Yes | `bought` or `cancel`. |
| `emailHash` | String | Conditional | MD5 hash of the buyer's email. **Required when status is `bought`**. |

### Behavior

- **`bought`**: Listing moves to `pendingVerification`. Balance is credited after automatic verification. User lock is released so you can request the next card.
- **`cancel`**: Lock is released, listing becomes available again.

request.description:
Returns {game, sets} with the full active current-season catalogue, without pagination. Each set contains setID, name, category, sourceUrl, catalogueHash, syncedAt (UTC), stale (boolean), and lineups. Each available lineup includes grade, tokens (estimated reward), totalPrice (estimated coins), and players with resourceID, name and price. No available lineups means an empty array; an empty catalogue returns sets: [].

Filtering is client-side; this action has no server-side filter parameters. Search name/category and compare lineup.totalPrice with your budget. To match the website, select each set's highest-token lineup (lowest price breaks ties), then apply the estimated budget filter. Top rewards only selects sets tied for the highest reward across all non-stale sets with lineups, before search/budget filtering. Sort by tokens, totalPrice, or totalPrice / tokens for positive token rewards. You may also inspect cheaper grades.

Exclude stale sets from purchase candidates: entries older than 24 hours cannot be purchased. Prices and rewards are estimates; account ownership of cards and historical Gallery progress are not included. With a price allowance, the required budget is the sum of min(15000000, floor(player.price * (100 + priceAllowancePercent) / 100)) over the selected lineup.

Set gallerySetId and galleryGrade from your chosen result, and galleryMaxCoins to your hard purchase budget. Create rechecks current prices and rejects a lineup whose buy limits exceed maxCoins. Do not pass catalogueHash or lineups to Create Gallery Order.

Creates an order using a server-resolved lineup. Required: requestID (UUID), setID, grade (D/C/B/A/S), account, accountType (sender/customer), maxCoins (total hard spending authorization). Optional: priceAllowancePercent (0-100, default 0), afterPurchase (keep/relist, default keep), resaleSteps (integer -100 to 100, default 0). If the sum of internal per-player caps exceeds maxCoins, creation is rejected. Returns buyTaskID. Identical retries reuse the frozen order even if the catalogue has refreshed; a changed setting with a reused requestID is rejected. No raw player array or catalogueHash is accepted.

resaleSteps applies to every card that is relisted and is measured from the price the order actually paid: 1 lists the card one EA price step above that price (the usual +1 offset), a negative number lists it below, and 0 keeps the unchanged purchase-price listing. Send it as a raw JSON number, never a quoted string: the body interpolates this collection's galleryResaleSteps variable as "resaleSteps": {{galleryResaleSteps}} (default 0). To try one step up, set galleryResaleSteps to 1 or send "resaleSteps": 1. A quoted value such as "1" is rejected because the server requires a JSON integer. One step is the EA price tier at that price, so the coins differ per card and one step does not guarantee covering EA's 5% market tax.

Queues 1-25 distinct sets for one owned EA account in the submitted order with action createBatch. Required: requestID (UUID), account, accountType (sender/customer), sets. sets is a native JSON array, not a quoted string: send it through this collection's galleryBasketSets variable, which interpolates the body as "sets": {{galleryBasketSets}}. Each entry has its own required maxCoins (integer 150-2147483647) that caps that set's resolved per-card limits, plus the same optional fields as Create Gallery Order: priceAllowancePercent (0-100, default 0), afterPurchase (keep/relist, default keep) and resaleSteps (integer -100 to 100, default 0, a JSON number). The optional top-level maxCoins caps the total of every resolved per-card limit across the basket and must be a raw JSON number; an omitted or null value leaves the per-set caps in charge.

The submitted order is the queue order, and the whole basket is validated before the first write: a stale set, a changed lineup, a duplicate set already queued for this account or one set over its own budget leaves nothing behind. Raw players, catalogueHash, payload, lineups and client-supplied ids such as batchID, buyTaskID, queueState or position are rejected at the basket level and in every entry.

Returns {"batchID":"...","buyTaskIDs":[...],"created":true} with buyTaskIDs ordered like sets. Retry an interrupted basket with the same requestID and an unchanged basket to receive the original batchID and ids with created false, even after the catalogue refreshed; changing the order, a grade, a budget, the account or a relist option with a reused requestID is rejected. This request stores batchID and its first buyTaskID in galleryBatchId and galleryBuyTaskId.
Returns the caller's latest 50 Gallery orders. Includes status, purchased/total counts, coin cost, set, grade and account.

Returns the owned order summary plus items and priceEditEligible. Each item includes resourceID, maxPrice, status, galleryStatus, galleryAction, pricePaid, resaleSteps and priceEditable. Resource IDs, coin limits and resaleSteps are integers; pricePaid and maxPrice may be null. resaleSteps is the persisted relist offset for that card (0 when the order has no custom setting) and only affects a card that is relisted. Internal purchased item IDs and snapshots are not returned. Existing queue metadata is retained.

Before editing, check order.priceEditEligible and select items with priceEditable=true. Copy the selected resourceID and current maxPrice into Edit Gallery Remaining Prices as resourceID and expectedMaxPrice, then choose the new maxPrice. Eligibility is rechecked at save time. Get Gallery Orders remains a summary-only list.

Change per-player hard limits on an existing stopped Gallery order. First run Get Gallery Order Progress and replace the sample resourceID and expectedMaxPrice with an editable player and its current maxPrice. Set maxPrice to the new authorized limit. The example raises one player from 300 to 600 coins.

prices is a native JSON array, not a quoted JSON string, with 1-200 entries. Each entry has exactly resourceID, maxPrice and expectedMaxPrice, all JSON integers (do not quote them). Resource IDs must be positive and unique; both limits must be between 150 and 15,000,000. Send only the remaining players you want to change; omitted players retain their limits.

If expectedMaxPrice no longer matches, the entire edit is rejected: fetch progress again and review the new values before retrying. Active or finished orders, worker-held orders, uncertain purchases and already bought/handled cards cannot be edited. Basket orders must be stopped with queueState waiting or blocked. Requests are restricted to the caller's own orders, including admin API identities.

Success: {"buyTaskID":"...","action":"editPrices"}. Saving does not resume the order. Run Resume Gallery Order separately after a successful save. New caps authorize a changed remaining budget; galleryMaxCoins/maxCoins limited the original creation and does not prevent this explicitly requested increase. Errors follow the existing HTTP-error/plain-text API convention.
Requests cancellation of this owned order. An in-flight operation may finish. Returns buyTaskID and action.

Queues unfinished work on this owned order, preserving completed purchases. Active/finished orders and unresolved purchases are rejected. Returns buyTaskID and action.

To retry after prices rise: Get Gallery Order Progress, Edit Gallery Remaining Prices, then run this request after the edit succeeds. The worker uses the saved limits; completed purchases stay preserved.

item.description:
Gallery catalogue and order API. Start with Get Gallery Sets / Catalogue to retrieve all active current-season sets, available grade lineups, estimated token rewards and player prices. Filter and sort the returned data in your code, then set gallerySetId and galleryGrade for Create Gallery Order. The server resolves the current lineup and enforces galleryMaxCoins when creating an order.

Run requests individually. Keep requestID unchanged when retrying an interrupted create; use a fresh UUID for a different order. New EA accounts use Order Management > Create New Customer first. apiUser/apiKey authentication follows SBC. Account and order access is restricted to the caller's own records.

To change prices on a stopped or partially completed order: Get Gallery Order Progress -> Edit Gallery Remaining Prices -> Resume Gallery Order. Review editable cards and current limits before saving. Editing does not resume automatically.

For a multi-set basket set galleryBasketSets to a JSON array of 1-25 entries (setID, grade and its own maxCoins, plus the optional priceAllowancePercent, afterPurchase and resaleSteps), optionally set galleryBasketMaxCoins for the total budget, then run Create Gallery Basket (action createBatch). It returns batchID, the ordered buyTaskIDs and created; retrying the same requestID with an unchanged basket returns the original ids with created false, even after the catalogue refreshed. Basket children report queuePosition, batchSize, queueState and queueNote in Get Gallery Orders; every action still targets one child buyTaskID. Do not send sets to Create Gallery Order.
